recipes.title: Crispy Lemon Butter Chicken
ingredients: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs — 6 medium / 800 g
Ground black pepper — 1 g / ½ tsp
Unsalted butter — 45 g / 3 tbsp, cubed and kept cold
Chicken stock — 120 ml / 8 tbsp / 0.42 UK cup / ½ US cup
Finely grated lemon zest — 2 g / 1 tsp
Plain flour — a little, for dusting the chicken (from the video)
To serve (from the video): mashed potato; broccoli florets cooked with 2 tbsp water, butter, salt and pepper
steps: 1. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then pat a little flour over both sides (the flour helps crisp the skin).
2. Mash or finely chop the garlic, chop the parsley, zest the lemon and squeeze about 2 tbsp juice.

3. Heat the olive oil and a little butter in a frying pan over a steady, medium heat. Add the chicken skin side down and cook for about 10 minutes, turning now and then, until golden and cooked through. Cook in batches if the pan is crowded.
4. Turn the thighs skin side down again for a final couple of minutes of colour, then rest them in a bowl to catch the juices.
5. Pour off most of the fat, leaving about a tablespoon. Fry the garlic gently without letting it burn.
6. Add the chicken stock and simmer for about 3 minutes until reduced by about half. Stir in the lemon juice, the resting juices and the lemon zest.
7. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cold butter a couple of cubes at a time, then the parsley, to make a runny lemon butter sauce.
8. Return the pan to a very low flame, put the chicken back in skin side up and warm for a couple of minutes. Don't spoon sauce over the skin until serving so it stays crisp.
9. Meanwhile microwave the broccoli florets with 2 tbsp water for about 3 minutes, drain, then toss with butter, salt and pepper.
10. Serve the chicken with mash and the broccoli, spooning the pan sauce over at the table.

recipes.title: Who Said French Cooking Was Hard? French Tacos
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast (1 lb 5 oz), cut into small strips
½ tsp ground black pepper (1 g)
200 ml double cream or heavy cream — ¾ US cup + 1 tbsp + 1 tsp; ⅔ UK cup + 2 tsp
100 g mature Cheddar, finely grated — a scant 1 US cup; ¾ UK cup
¼ tsp ground black pepper (0.5 g)
GLUE: 1-2  tbsp flour 1 tbsp water mix
steps: 1. Cook the frozen chips in the air fryer at about 215–220°C for about 20 minutes, until lightly coloured but still soft.
2. Slice the chicken breast into thin strips and toss in a bowl with the salt, pepper, oregano, paprika (smoked or sweet), cumin and garlic powder.
3. Make the burger sauce: mix the mayonnaise, ketchup and yellow mustard and set aside.
4. Heat the oil in a pan and fry the chicken in two batches until coloured and just cooked. Don't overcook the strips.
5. For the cheese sauce, warm the cream gently without boiling, add the black pepper, then melt in the grated Cheddar until pourable but thick. Take off the heat.
6. Mix 1–2 tbsp flour with 1 tbsp water to make a paste 'glue' (optional).
7. Lay out each wrap, spread burger sauce in the middle, then add chips, hot chicken and some cheese sauce, keeping the filling central.
8. Brush the flour glue on the edges, fold the sides in and the top and bottom over to make a sealed parcel.
9. Toast the parcels seam side down on a hot plate, griddle or dry frying pan until golden and marked, then turn and toast the other side.
10. Serve with extra cheese sauce. Tip: if the cheese sauce won't thicken, stir in 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with water.

recipes.title: One Pack of Mince, a Whole Pan of Dinner
ingredients: 2 medium onions, cut into chunky wedges
300 g (10½ oz) carrots, cut into thick chunks
1 kg (2 lb 3 oz) potatoes, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm (1-inch) chunks
2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, to finish
To serve (from the video): a small cabbage, sliced, microwaved with 2 tbsp water, then butter, salt and pepper
steps: 1. Cut the carrots into rustic chunks, the onions into wedges and the potatoes into roughly 2 cm cubes.
2. Heat the oil in a large pan and add the beef mince (it can go in frozen). Season with salt and pepper and cook until the water has cooked out and the mince has a little colour.
3. Add the onion wedges and carrot chunks and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, to start softening.
4. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute, then stir in the tomato purée and cook for a minute.
5. Stir in the flour (about 3 level tablespoons) and cook for about a minute.
6. Add the Worcestershire sauce, then the beef stock, scraping up the bits on the bottom of the pan. Add the bay leaf and thyme.

7. Add the potatoes, bring to a simmer, cover and cook for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes and carrots are tender. Add a splash of water if the gravy gets too thick or starts to stick.
8. Meanwhile microwave the sliced cabbage with 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes, stir, then 4 minutes more. Stir in butter, salt and pepper, cover and let it steam for a minute.
9. Remove the bay leaf, check the seasoning, scatter over the parsley and serve with the buttered cabbage.

recipes.title: Spaghetti & Meatball Soup — Yes, I Broke It!
ingredients: 30 g dried breadcrumbs — ⅓ US cup / a generous ¼ UK cup
2 tbsp tomato purée — 30 g; concentrated tomato paste in the US
2 × 400 g tins chopped tomatoes — 800 g total
750 ml beef or chicken stock — 3⅛ US cups / 2⅔ UK cups
100 g dried spaghetti, broken into short lengths
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Fresh basil and grated Parmesan, to serve, optional
steps: 1. Dice the onion, coarsely grate the carrot and grate or mince the garlic, keeping 2 cloves for the meatballs and the rest for the soup.
2. Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for a moment, then mix with the beef mince, beaten egg, 2 grated garlic cloves, oregano, salt and pepper.
3. Roll into small meatballs (about 26–28) and set them on a tray.
4. Heat the olive oil in a large pan and fry the meatballs in batches just until coloured all over. They don't need to be cooked through. Set aside and pour off most of the oil.
5. Fry the onion, then the carrot, until lightly coloured. Add the remaining garlic for about 30 seconds.
6. Stir in the tomato purée and cook briefly, then the sugar if using.

7. Add the tomatoes (chop whole ones in the pan), oregano, a little salt and black pepper, then the stock. Simmer gently, stirring now and then. Add water or more stock if it gets too thick, as this should be a soup.
8. Blend the soup with a stick blender, as smooth or chunky as you like.
9. Return the meatballs and simmer for at least 5 minutes.
10. Break the spaghetti into short lengths, stir it in and simmer for about 10–12 minutes until tender, stirring so it doesn't stick.
11. In the last minute, stir through torn basil and a little Parmesan. Serve topped with more Parmesan and basil.

recipes.title: REAL UK HOT DOGS! — We Batter Ours!
ingredients: 150 g self-raising flour — 1¼ US cups / 1 UK cup + 1 tbsp, plus extra for dusting
¼ tsp food-grade citric acid — 1 g
¼ tsp fine salt — 1.5 g, plus extra for serving
200 ml water — 13⅓ tbsp / 0.85 US cup / 0.70 UK cup
Rice flour, for coating the sausages before battering (used in the video)
Butter, for the rolls (from the video)
steps: 1. Put the sausages in an oven tray with a little oil and cook at 190°C for about 20 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and cooked through.
2. Let the sausages cool for 7–8 minutes, pat off the fat with kitchen paper, then coat them in rice flour so the batter will stick.
3. Make the batter: whisk the self-raising flour (about 150 g), salt and warm water into a smooth batter. Don't add the citric acid yet.
4. Heat the oil for deep-frying to 175–180°C, filling the pan only about one third full. Set a rack over kitchen paper on a tray.
5. About a minute before frying, whisk the citric acid into the batter. It fizzes and makes the batter lighter and crispier, so don't mix it in ahead of time.
6. Dip the sausages in the batter and fry a few at a time until crisp and golden, patching any bare spots with extra batter. Fry a few drips of batter for 'scraps'.
7. Drain on the rack and let them rest for a minute.
8. Split and butter the rolls, add some scraps and a battered sausage, then season with malt vinegar, salt and ketchup. Serve with mushy peas.

recipes.title: Creamy Shredded Chicken Curry – Chicken Bharta
ingredients: Cooked rotisserie chicken, skin and bones removed – 600 g, coarsely shredded
Full-fat plain yoghurt, beaten – 100 g / 6 tbsp + 2 tsp
Double cream or heavy cream – 60 ml / 4 tbsp / ¼ US cup / 0.21 UK cup
Water for the gravy – 120 ml / 8 tbsp / ½ US cup / 0.42 UK cup
Hard-boiled eggs – 2, one chopped and one quartered
Hot water for soaking – 120 ml; discard after soaking
Fresh water for blending – 45 ml / 3 tbsp
Fine salt – ½ tsp / 3 g, then adjust to taste
Chicken stock — 1 chicken stock cube dissolved in water, or plain water (used in the video for the gravy)
Black pepper — a little (added in the video; not in the description)
steps: 1. Shred the cooked chicken. Blend the tomatoes to a purée (or finely chop them).
2. Soak the cashews in hot water, drain, then blend with about 3 tbsp fresh water to a thick paste. Hard-boil the eggs.
3. Finely chop the onions, green chillies and coriander.
4. Heat the oil and butter (or ghee) in a pan, add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cardamom and cinnamon, then the onion. Cook for 6–8 minutes, or up to 10–12, until golden.
5. Add the garlic and ginger paste and the green chilli and cook for about a minute.
6. Lower the heat and add the ground coriander, cumin, Kashmiri chilli, salt, turmeric and a little black pepper. Stir for a minute to bloom the spices.
7. Add the tomato, raise the heat and cook for about 8 minutes into a thick paste until the raw tomato smell has gone and oil starts to separate. Add a spoonful of stock if it catches.
8. Turn the heat low and stir in the cashew paste a spoonful at a time, letting it cook for a minute.
9. Stir in the remaining stock or water, then remove the bay leaf, cinnamon and cardamom if you like.
10. Add the shredded chicken, then the cream. Stir in one chopped boiled egg and heat gently for 5–7 minutes until the chicken is hot through, adding water if it gets too thick.
11. Turn off the heat and stir in the coriander, kasuri methi and garam masala. Serve topped with the quartered egg.

recipes.title: Chicken Coq au Vin Without the Long Wait
ingredients: Plain flour, for dusting — 2 tbsp / 16 g
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 medium red onion or 3 shallots, finely diced — 150 g
Dry red wine — 500 ml / 2 US cups / 1¾ UK cups
Chicken stock — 300 ml / 1¼ US cups / 1 UK cup + 1 tbsp
Bouquet garni — 3 thyme sprigs, 1 bay leaf and a few parsley stalks, tied together
Jarred pickled silverskin onions, drained weight — 200 g / 1¼ US cups or 1 UK cup
Button mushrooms, left whole if small or halved — 250 g
steps: 1. Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper, dust with flour on both sides and leave skin side up for about 5 minutes while you prep the veg.
2. Tie the thyme, bay leaf and parsley stalks into a bouquet garni. Drain the pickled silverskin onions, soak them in water for a while to remove some vinegar, then drain and pat dry.
3. Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery, chop 3 garlic cloves and thinly slice the other 2. Halve any large mushrooms.

4. Heat the oven to 200°C. Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken skin side down for about 4–5 minutes until golden, then a couple of minutes on the other side. Rest on a tray.
5. Fry the bacon lardons in the same pan until browned, then lift them out.
6. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 5–6 minutes to soften. Add the chopped garlic for about 30 seconds.
7. Lower the heat a little and stir in the tomato purée for about a minute, then 1 tbsp flour for about a minute.
8. Pour in the red wine gradually, add the bouquet garni and simmer until reduced by about half.
9. Add the chicken stock and simmer for about 15 minutes until reduced by half and the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
10. Meanwhile roast the chicken in the oven for about 15 minutes until cooked through, then rest.
11. In another pan, fry the silverskin onions in a little olive oil over moderate heat, then add some butter and the sliced garlic for about a minute. Lift out.
12. Fry the mushrooms until coloured, add the remaining butter, then return the bacon, onions and garlic. Take off the heat and stir in the parsley.
13. Strain the sauce to remove the veg and herbs.
14. Slice the chicken thickly and serve on mashed potato with the bacon, onion and mushroom garnish and the red wine sauce.

ingredients: Onion, finely chopped — 150 g / ⅝ UK cup / ¾ US cup
Frozen peas, thawed — 100 g / ½ UK cup / ⅔ US cup
Fresh ginger, finely grated — 1 tbsp / 6 g
Fine salt — ¾ tsp / 4.5 g, plus extra for the skins
Plain yoghurt — 120 g / 8 tbsp / 0.42 UK cup / ½ US cup
Fresh mint, finely chopped — 1 tbsp / 3 g
Tamarind chutney — 4 tbsp / 60 ml / 0.21 UK cup / ¼ US cup
Water — 150 ml (10 tbsp / 30 tsp / 0.53 UK cup / 0.63 US cup)
Soft brown sugar — 60 g (5 packed tbsp / ¼ UK cup / ⅓ US cup)
Salt or black salt — ¼ tsp
Cornflour (cornstarch) — a little, mixed with water to thicken the chutney (used in the video)
steps: 1. Wash the potatoes, prick them all over, score a line around each one and microwave in a covered container on high for about 12–14 minutes until tender. Heat the oven to about 220°C.
2. Heat the ghee in a pan, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle, then fry the onion until lightly golden.
3. Turn down the heat and add the ginger and green chillies, then the ground coriander and turmeric. Stir to bloom the spices.
4. Add the peas and cook for just a couple of minutes. Take off the heat.
5. Brush the potato skins with ghee, rub with salt and bake for about 15 minutes to crisp the skins.
6. For the mint yoghurt, mix the yoghurt with the mint, lemon juice and salt, then chill.

7. For the tamarind chutney, simmer the tamarind paste, water, brown sugar, cumin, ginger, chilli powder and salt until the sugar dissolves. Thicken with a little cornflour slurry. Add water if it gets too thick, as it should be runny.
8. Stir the fresh coriander, garam masala and lemon juice into the pea filling.
9. Microwave the poppadoms for about 30–40 seconds until puffed, then crush them roughly.
10. When the potatoes are cool enough to handle, scoop out the flesh, mix it with the filling (mashed or chunky), taste for salt and pile it back into the skins.
11. Brush the tops with melted ghee and bake for 20–25 minutes until crisp.
12. Serve topped with mint yoghurt, tamarind chutney and crushed poppadoms.

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Blackberry Jam Roly Poly
ingredients: Self-raising flour — 2 cups / 250 g, plus extra for dusting
Shredded beef or vegetable suet — 1 cup / 125 g
Milk — 10 tbsp / 150 ml, adding only as needed
Thick blackberry jam — ⅔ cup / 200 g
Softened butter — 1 tsp / 5 g, for greasing the baking paper
For the crust (from the video): a little extra butter for brushing and a sprinkling of sugar
Water — boiling, a couple of centimetres in a tray for steaming
steps: 1. Mix the self-raising flour, salt and sugar in a bowl, then stir in the suet (grate it from frozen if it's soft).
2. Add the milk gradually and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
3. Lay a sheet of parchment over a sheet of foil and brush the parchment with butter.
4. Stir the jam with a spoon until spreadable. Don't warm it.
5. On a floured surface, roll the dough to a rectangle of about 25 × 30 cm, keeping an even thickness.
6. Spread the jam over the dough, leaving a border. Brush water along the edges to seal.
7. Roll up loosely from the short side and place seam side down on the buttered parchment. Wrap loosely in the parchment and foil, leaving room to expand.
8. Put a tray on the lowest shelf of the oven with a couple of centimetres of boiling water to make steam. Bake the roly poly on the shelf above at about 180–200°C for about 45 minutes.
9. Open the parcel, brush the top with butter, sprinkle with sugar and bake for another 10 minutes for a crusty top.
10. Rest for 10 minutes, then slice and serve with warm custard.

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Rissoles with Diane Sauce
ingredients: Onion — ½ medium / 75 g, finely grated and excess juice squeezed out
Garlic — 2 cloves / 2 tsp / 6 g, finely grated
Ground black pepper — ½ tsp / 1 g
Plain flour — ¼ cup / 4 tbsp / 35 g
Neutral oil — 7–10 tbsp / 105–150 ml, for shallow frying
Onion — ½ medium / 75 g, finely chopped
Garlic — 2 cloves / 2 tsp / 6 g, finely chopped
Tomato purée / concentrated tomato paste — 1 tsp / 5 g
Ground black pepper — ¼ tsp / 0.5 g
steps: 1. Halve the onion: grate one half for the rissoles and squeeze out the excess juice, and finely chop the other half for the sauce. Split the garlic between the rissoles and the sauce. Thickly slice the mushrooms.
2. Mix the chicken mince with the grated onion, garlic, beaten egg, Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, pepper and panko. Add more panko if the mix is too wet. Rest for 10 minutes.
3. Divide into 8, shape into patties on a parchment-lined tray and chill for about 30 minutes.
4. For the sauce, heat a pan with just a smear of butter and fry the mushrooms without seasoning until deeply browned.
5. Lower the heat, add the rest of the butter and the chopped onion and soften for about 3 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
6. Stir in the tomato purée for about a minute. Off the heat, add the brandy (optional) and cook it out.
7. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon (about 2 tsp) and black pepper, then the cream. Simmer for a few minutes, season and keep warm. Add the parsley before serving.
8. Set up a flour, egg-and-water and panko station. Coat each rissole in flour, then egg, then panko, and set on a rack.

9. Heat the oil for shallow frying over moderate heat (not too hot) and fry the rissoles for about 3–5 minutes, turning a couple of times, until golden and cooked through. Fry in batches and drain on a rack.
10. Serve the rissoles with the Diane sauce and sides such as peas or mash.

ingredients: Potatoes: 900 g / 2 lb, peeled and cut into 1.5–2 cm cubes
Beef mince: 500 g / 1 lb 2 oz, ideally 10–15% fat
Onion, finely chopped: 1 medium, 150 g | 1 US cup | ⅚ UK cup
Frozen mixed vegetables: 500 g | 3½ US cups | 3 UK cups
Butter: 30 g |  2 tbsp | ⅛ US cup | ⅒ UK cup

recipes.title: Creamy Bacon & Pea Barley Risotto
ingredients: 300g pearl barley — , rinsed and drained  1½ US cups / 1¼ UK imperial cups
200g smoked streaky bacon, cut into small pieces
200g frozen peas — 1½ US cups / 1¼ UK imperial cups
40g finely grated Parmesan — ½ US cup / just under ½ UK imperial cup, loosely filled
100ml dry white wine, or extra stock
1,300ml hot chicken or vegetable stock, preferably low salt—you may not need it all
steps: 1. Rinse the pearl barley. Dice the onion and chop the garlic.

4. Add the barley and stir for a couple of minutes to coat it in the fat.

8. Stir in the bacon and frozen peas for a couple of minutes, then turn off the heat.
9. Stir in the remaining butter (about 1 tbsp) and the black pepper, then the Parmesan. Taste before adding any salt.
10. Serve topped with the reserved crispy bacon, with crusty bread or buttered toast.

steps: 1. Heat the oven to 180°C and line the base of an 8-inch (20 cm) cake tin. A 9-inch tin also works.

ingredients: 1 or 2 very large floury potato, about 600 g / 21 oz

steps: 1. Make the dressing: mix the ketchup, mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper, mustard, 2 tbsp chopped pickles and the pickle liquor. Chill.

3. Cut the potatoes into thick slices (two per burger), cover with water, bring to the boil and cook for about 6–8 minutes until just starting to soften but not crumbling.
4. Cool the slices in cold water, drain and pat dry with kitchen paper.
5. Dust a tray with rice flour. Sandwich some tuna mix between two potato slices, press firmly and dust with rice flour. Chill for about 30 minutes to firm up.
6. Make the batter: mix the plain flour, rice flour, baking powder, salt, a little turmeric and pepper, then whisk in the water to a thickish batter. Leave out the citric acid for now.
7. Heat the frying oil to about 180°C. Just before frying, whisk in the citric acid. It fizzes and makes the batter lighter.
8. Dip each scallop in the batter and deep-fry until crisp and golden, frying a few drips of batter for scraps.
9. Toast the burger buns, spread with the dressing, add a scallop and some more dressing, then serve.

recipes.title: A Rich Bolognese ..You Can Afford

recipes.title: Two Takeaway Favourites, One Wok
ingredients: Beef, Black Bean and Garlic Stir-Fry:
400 g beef, thinly sliced against the grain
1 tbsp Lee Kum Kee Black Bean Garlic Sauce (about 17 g)
½ tsp dark soy sauce (2.5 ml)
1 tbsp Chinese cooking wine/Shaoxing wine (15 ml)
75 ml water (5 tbsp; about ⅓ US cup or ⅓ UK cup)
A pinch of MSG, optional (about ⅛ tsp)
A pinch of white pepper (about ⅛ tsp)
Only if needed: 1 tsp potato starch (about 3 g), mixed with 1 tbsp cold water (15 ml)
King Prawns with Chilli Bean Sauce:
400 g (14 oz) raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
1 medium onion, sliced, about 150 g (roughly 1 UK cup / 1 US cup)
1 medium carrot, thinly sliced, about 100 g (roughly ¾ UK cup / ¾ US cup)
1 green pepper, sliced, about 150 g (roughly 1 UK cup / 1 US cup)
1 tsp (about 6 g) Lee Kum Kee chilli bean sauce
A small pinch of MSG, optional
steps: 1. Taste the black bean garlic and chilli bean sauces first, as both are very salty. Use them sparingly, about a teaspoon if unsure.
2. Beef: heat a wide wok until very hot, add a little oil, lower the flame and stir-fry the thinly sliced beef until browned. Remove to a bowl.
3. Add a little more oil and stir-fry the diced onion, green pepper and chilli, then the grated ginger.
4. Return the beef and add the black bean garlic sauce, the water, dark soy, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper, Shaoxing wine and a few drops of sesame oil (plus MSG if using). Stir to coat.

8. Add the chilli bean sauce (a heaped teaspoon at most), the water, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, MSG (optional), white pepper and sesame oil. Add the prawns and toss to coat. Use a tiny bit of starch slurry to make it sticky if you like.
9. Turn off the heat and serve both dishes with rice to balance the salt and heat.

recipes.title: The Easiest Full Tray Pizza You’ll Ever Make

recipes.title: How I Make 150g Mince Feed Six or EIGHT... You Can Afford

200 g mushrooms, finely chopped —  2½ US cups / 2 UK cups
200 g onion, finely diced — 1⅓ US cups / 1 UK cup
150 g carrots, finely diced — 1 US cup / ¾ UK cup
15 g beef dripping, butter, tallow or lard — 1 US or UK tbsp, if needed
30 g tomato purée — 2 US or UK tbsp
18 g plain flour — 2 US or UK tbsp
450 ml reduced-salt beef stock — 1⅞ US cups / 1⅗ UK cups
15 ml Worcestershire sauce — 1 US or UK tbsp

5 ml balsamic vinegar — 1 US or UK tsp
1 g dried thyme — 1 US or UK tsp

3 g garlic powder — 1 US or UK tsp

recipes.title: Sausage Rolls...You Can Afford
ingredients: This makes enough filling for approximately 16 substantial sausage rolls.
100g dry fine TVP — ¾ UK cup / 1 US cup
180ml boiling water -  ⅔ UK cup / ¾ US cup
½–1 tsp pork or chicken stock powder, depending on saltiness —  2–4g
50g dry red lentils — ¼ UK cup / ¼ US cup
100g onion, extremely finely diced — ½ UK cup / ⅔ US cup
75g button mushrooms, chopped into tiny granules —  ¾ UK cup / 1 US cup
40g softened lard for the filling — 3 tbsp
40g fine breadcrumbs — ⅓ UK cup / ⅖ US cup
Salt only after cooking a test piece
Ready-rolled puff pastry (used in the video)
Beaten egg, for sealing and glazing (from the video)
steps: 1. Blitz some of the TVP finely so the texture is more like sausage meat, then mix it with the rest.

2. Dissolve the pork or chicken stock powder in the boiling water and stir in the gelatine (optional) until it dissolves. Pour over the TVP and leave for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Don't add salt if the stock is salty.
3. Chop the mushrooms into tiny granules and dice the onion extremely finely.
4. Boil the rinsed red lentils for 6–8 minutes, drain without rinsing and mash lightly.
5. Heat a little lard and gently cook the onion (and mushrooms) for about 4–5 minutes until soft and golden. Spread on a tray to cool.
6. Add 1 tbsp lard to the pan and cook the TVP over a very low flame for just 3–4 minutes without browning. Cool.
7. Mix the sausage seasoning: sage, thyme, onion powder, mustard powder, white pepper, mace, nutmeg, black pepper, sugar and MSG (optional).
8. Combine the onion and lentils with the TVP, seasoning, breadcrumbs and wheat gluten. Add the egg, Worcestershire sauce and softened lard, and work by hand for about 2 minutes until tacky.
9. Chill for about 1 hour so the breadcrumbs rehydrate. Fry a test piece and add salt only if needed.
10. Heat the oven to about 190–200°C. Roll the filling into sausage shapes, lay on puff pastry, brush the edge with beaten egg, roll over and seal. Cut to size.
11. Brush with beaten egg and cut vent holes in the top.
12. Bake on a lower-middle shelf for about 25–32 minutes until golden. Rest for 5 minutes, then cool on a rack.

ingredients: 100 g finely chopped cabbage removed from the centres — approx ¾ UK cup or 1 US cup

steps: 1. Boil the whole cabbages in salted water, covered, for 8–10 minutes to soften, then drain and cool in cold water until you can handle them.

3. Cut a cone out of the centre of each cabbage, angling towards the core. Squeeze out the absorbed water by turning them upside down and pressing gently.

5. Fry the onion in the oil and a little butter, add the chopped cabbage for about 5–7 minutes, then the garlic for about a minute. Cool.
6. Mix the beef mince with the cooked rice, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper, salt, paprika, oregano and egg, then stir in the cooled cabbage mixture.
7. Heat the oven to 190°C. Pour some sauce into a baking dish, sit the cabbages in it and pack the filling into the centres. Pour the rest of the sauce around so it comes about halfway up.
8. Put the dish on a tray, cover tightly with foil and bake for about 1 hour 10–15 minutes. The filling should reach 71°C (160°F).

ingredients: 500 g beef liver, sliced into 1 cm strips

4. Add the onions to the bacon fat with the butter and the brown sugar (optional) and cook for 10–12 minutes until soft and caramelised. Lift out the bacon and onions.
5. Season the flour with the salt and pepper and toss the dry liver in it, shaking off the excess.
6. Heat the oil and a little butter in a hot pan and sear the liver in batches for about 60 seconds per side until golden. Set aside.

ingredients: 5 large eggs, about 250 g without shells

¼ tsp fine salt, about 1.5 g
¼ tsp black pepper, about 0.6 g

steps: 1. Finely chop the spring onion or chives.
2. Put the eggs in a pan of water, bring to the boil and boil for about 9 minutes. Cool under running cold water for 5 minutes, then peel.
3. Separate the yolks from the whites. Roughly chop the whites.

recipes.title: Put The OOH In Batter
ingredients: 150 g plain flour — approximately 1 UK cup or 1¼ US cups
⅛ tsp citric acid — approximately 0.5 g
200–225 ml room-temperature water — approximately ¾–⅞ UK cup or ¾ cup plus 2½ tbsp–1 US cup
Plain flour — a little extra, for dusting what you're battering (from the video)
To batter (as in the video): onion rings, fish fillets or a burger
steps: 1. Prepare what you're battering, e.g. slice a red onion into rings, and dust it lightly with plain flour so the batter sticks. Don't season the onion rings, or they will sweat.
2. Mix the plain flour, baking powder and salt (or use self-raising flour and salt).
3. Whisk in the room-temperature water (about 26–28°C) to make a smooth batter.
4. Heat the oil to 180°C. The oil must be ready before the last step.
5. When the oil is hot, whisk the ⅛ tsp citric acid into the batter. It reacts with the baking powder and makes CO₂ instantly for a light, crisp coating. Too much citric acid will make it sour.
6. Dip the floured items in the batter and fry straight away, turning, until golden and crisp.
7. Drain on a rack over a tray and serve.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken and Bacon Cobbler with Cheese Scones
ingredients: 700 g chicken breast, cut into 4 cm / 1½-inch chunks
200 g smoked bacon, cut into strips
300 g mushrooms, thickly sliced — 3 UK cups / 3¼ US cups
200 g onion, diced — ¾ UK cup / ⅞ US cup

40 g butter — 3 tbsp / 8 tsp / ⅙ cup
40 g plain flour — 4½ tbsp / 13½ tsp / ⅓ cup

150 ml double or heavy cream — 10 tbsp / 30 tsp / ⅗ UK cup / ⅔ US cup

steps: 1. Dice the onion, thickly slice the mushrooms (halve small ones), mince the garlic, chop the parsley and cut the chicken into chunks.
2. Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the chicken, seasoning it with a little thyme and pepper. It doesn't need to cook through. Set aside.
3. Add the onions and bacon and cook until starting to colour, using the bacon fat.
4. Add a little of the butter and the mushrooms and brown them, then the garlic and the remaining dried thyme.

8. For the scones, mix the self-raising flour, baking powder and salt, then rub in the cold butter. Dissolve the mustard (powder or prepared) in the cold milk, add it and mix to a rough dough, then work in the grated Cheddar.
9. On a lightly floured surface, pat the dough to about 2.5 cm (1 inch) thick without rolling, and cut out about 8 scones, or break off rough pieces.
10. Set the scones on the filling, pressing them in gently. Brush with milk and top with the extra Cheddar.
11. Bake for about 20–25 minutes until the scones are puffed and golden and the sauce is bubbling. The video doesn't state an oven temperature.
